identity.description:
Write eval baselines at two repeats

## Summary

This PR records two eval decisions in the docs. It changes no code.

- A new baseline is written at two repeats, not three. Two repeats give the spread that the margin rule needs, at less cost.
- A routine eval against the baseline stays at one repeat.
- To cut noise, the case set grows before the repeat count does. More cases reduce the noise of one case and the noise between runs. More repeats reduce only the noise between runs. In the D7 evals, one case moved precision by 0.1 between two runs of nearly the same code.

The README baseline section, design section 8 and the D4b ticket now say this. The CI eval job keeps `--repeat 3`, because a change to it is a workflow change.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` passes.
- [x] `scripts/check-version-bump.sh` says the change touches no shipped file.

findings.span_text: - Metrics: grounded recall on posted goldens only, and two precisions on posted findings. Strict precision counts the matches only. Adjudicated precision also counts the posted findings with no golden that the extras judge accepts as real defects under the severity policy. The accepted extras go to `candidates.json` for a person to review, and `golden.json` does not change. A posted finding that matches a not-real golden is a false positive. Raw recall scores the reviewer findings before the verifier, the merge and the cap, so the gap to recall shows what the pipeline dropped. Without `--raw-judge`, raw recall sends no judge query: it takes exact matches and the judge answers that the posted pass already got. The drop counts give the dropped findings by stage, from the rows of `pr-review explain`. Also findings per PR, and the cost per PR of the review run and of the judge. Run each case three times and report the spread. The eval pools the precision of a repeat over the cases: the matched posted findings divided by all posted findings. - Gate: a change that touches behaviour runs the eval locally at one repeat against `eval/baseline.json`, and the PR description carries the table. A new baseline runs at two repeats, so the margins rest on a measured spread. To cut noise, the set grows before the repeat count does: with ten cases, one case moved precision by 0.1 between two runs of nearly the same code. The eval job in CI runs on manual dispatch only. The gate fails when recall or precision drops past the margin of the baseline. One contributor works on the repo, so the eval does not run on every PR; a run over ten cases costs about $40 at one repeat.
